statements.proposition: In this change, template_to_pic falls back to file://{template_path} as the page URL when the caller provides no base_url, preserving the old behaviour.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Partly true only: the fallback file://{template_path} applies when the caller passes a pages dict without base_url. When the caller omits pages (the common default call), the function's own default pages dict at head sets base_url=f'file://{getcwd()}', so page_base_url becomes file://{cwd}, not file://{template_path}. At base, html_to_pic was always called with template_path=f'file://{template_path}'. So the default call no longer navigates to file://{template_path}; the stated backward-compatible default does not hold for that case.
evidence: head fd64c2a data_source.py template_to_pic: 'if pages is None: pages = {"viewport": ..., "base_url": f"file://{getcwd()}"}' then 'page_base_url = pages.get("base_url", f"file://{template_path}")' and html_to_pic(template_path=page_base_url, ...)
base 160fffd data_source.py template_to_pic: same default pages dict, but html_to_pic(template_path=f"file://{template_path}", ...) unconditionally
html_to_pic does page.goto(template_path) then page.set_content(html), so the goto URL is the document URL

statements.proposition: This change is fully backward compatible: all existing code continues to work without modification.
statements.label: CANNOT_TELL
statements.note: Signatures and names are unchanged and the removed file:// check only loosens html_to_pic. But there is a concrete default-behaviour change: template_to_pic called without pages now navigates to file://{getcwd()} instead of file://{template_path}, which changes how relative resources in templates resolve; also pages with base_url=None would now pass None to page.goto. Whether existing callers actually break depends on their templates; not demonstrated by running (needs Playwright browser). Leaning false, not settled.

Repository callers (example/plugins/render/__init__.py, tests) pass base_url=f'file://{template_path}' explicitly, so they are unaffected
